scan.1: Rarely looks before receiving; discovers the pressure when the ball arrives.
scan.2: Looks before receiving when there is time, rarely under pressure.
scan.3: Looks before every touch and knows where the nearest opponent is.
scan.4: Scans several times before receiving and is already playing the next option.

controle.1: Stops the ball under the feet or lets it get away.
controle.2: Takes a directional touch without pressure, often with the same foot.
controle.3: Takes the first touch into space, with both feet, under pressure.
controle.4: The first touch beats an opponent or opens the next pass straight away.

passe.1: Passes to the nearest teammate, with no visible purpose.
passe.2: Passes accurately and serves a purpose when there is time.
passe.3: Picks the pass that serves the purpose of the moment, to the right foot, at the right pace.
passe.4: The pass creates the next action: breaks a line, draws pressure or frees a teammate.

conduite.1: Carries with the head down; the ball drifts away from the foot.
conduite.2: Carries with the head up into open space, with no opponent close.
conduite.3: Carries to progress or to draw, changes pace and direction.
conduite.4: The carry breaks a line or pulls an opponent out, then the ball is released at the right moment.

dribble-njangi.1: Avoids one against one, or dribbles without looking at teammates.
dribble-njangi.2: Tries one against one and sometimes wins, without seeing what comes next.
dribble-njangi.3: Dribbles to draw two opponents, then plays the freed teammate.
dribble-njangi.4: Picks the moment to beat, pin or release; the dribble pays the team.

appels.1: Stands still or follows the ball when not in possession.
appels.2: Makes runs to receive, mostly towards the ball.
appels.3: Also makes runs that free a teammate or stretch the defence.
appels.4: Reads the game before others: the runs open the decisive passing lane.

communication.2: Calls for the ball and sometimes encourages.
communication.3: Gives short, useful information to the ball carrier and nearby teammates.
communication.4: Organises teammates, guides the rest defence and the press, calms the group.

protection.1: Loses the ball at the first contact.
protection.2: Shields the ball with the body when standing still.
protection.3: Shields on the move, feels the opponent and turns away into space.
protection.4: Keeps the ball under pressure from two opponents and draws them to free a teammate.

contre-pression.1: Stops or complains after losing the ball.
contre-pression.2: Reacts to the loss, but alone or late.
contre-pression.3: Presses straight after the loss, closing a passing lane.
contre-pression.4: Triggers and organises the team's counter-press, and knows when to drop.

decision.1: Always makes the same choice, whatever the situation.
decision.2: Makes the right choice with time and little pressure.
decision.3: Makes the right choice under pressure and can explain the intention.
decision.4: Chooses quickly and well, even tired or trailing, and makes others play better.

possession.title: Possession
possession.q: How do we build out, where do we pin, where do we want to finish?

transitionDef.title: Defensive transition
transitionDef.q: What do we do in the seconds after losing the ball?

defense.title: Defending
defense.q: How high do we defend, when do we press?

transitionOff.title: Attacking transition
transitionOff.q: What do we do right after winning the ball?

setPieces.title: Set pieces
setPieces.q: Corners, free kicks, throw-ins: who does what?

possession: Build out with three, the pivot between the centre-backs
The goalkeeper is our first passer
Wingers stay glued to the touchline
Receive between the lines, facing forward
Breathe when leading: keep the ball, make them run
transitionDef: Closest player presses, the others close the middle
If we cannot win it back, drop quickly behind the ball
defense: Mid block, compact between the lines
Press high on the goalkeeper's restarts
No more than 30 m from defence to attack
transitionOff: Look forward: the first look goes in behind
Wingers attack the space in behind
First pass forward if it is on
If nothing is open, secure it and breathe
setPieces: Inswinging corners, two players at the near post
Rest defence of 3 on our corners
Free kicks: one short routine, one direct delivery
Quick throw-ins to the free player
Their corners: two players zonal, the rest man to man

levelHint.1: The behaviour is absent or rare.
levelHint.2: It shows when the player has time and little pressure.
levelHint.3: It is consistent in matches, under pressure.
levelHint.4: It makes the difference and makes others play better.

skillDef.scan: Looking around before receiving to know where teammates, opponents and space are.
skillDef.controle: Receiving the ball into open space or into the next action, instead of stopping it.
skillDef.passe: A pass that serves one of the five intentions, to the right teammate, foot and pace.
skillDef.conduite: Moving forward with the ball to progress or draw an opponent, head up, ball close.
skillDef.dribble-njangi: Dribbling to draw, pin, then release or beat: an investment, not a show.
skillDef.appels: Moving without the ball to receive, free a teammate, stretch the defence or open a lane.
skillDef.communication: Short, useful information at the right moment, by voice or gesture.
skillDef.protection: Keeping the ball under pressure with body, footwork and orientation.
skillDef.contre-pression: Reacting straight after the loss to win the ball back within 5 seconds.
skillDef.decision: Choosing, at the right moment, the option that best serves the team.
